title: docs(report-schema): drop the retired `onSave` / `onCancel` and put the Report Builder example under `check:doc-snippets`
body:
Fixes #7488

`ReportBuilderSchema.onSave` / `.onCancel` have been `?: never` on the TypeScript face and
`handlerKeyRefusal(...)` arms on the zod mirror since PR objectui#7468 (objectui#7344, in the
objectui#6124 shape). The Report Builder example on `content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx`
still authored both, so the page taught a literal that is a `tsc` assignment error **and** a
named `safeParse` refusal. The two lines are removed — the disposition objectui#7340 chose
for seven of its eight pages.

The example is not hollow without them: the section teaches the `ReportBuilderSchema` shape
(`type`, `report`, `availableFields`, `showPreview`), not a save/cancel flow.

## ⭐ Why nothing went red, measured rather than asserted

Three instruments were green **while the defect was present**, each for its own reason:

| instrument | why it could not see the line |
|:--|:--|
| `check:doc-snippets` | compiles `ts` / `tsx` fences only — this block was ```plaintext |
| `check:doc-types` | reads `type` string literals, nothing else |
| `component-docs-retired-handler-keys-7340.test.ts` | its `DOC_MEMBER_RE` requires `key?: type` (a member DECLARATION row) or a markdown prop-table row; the example's `onSave: 'handleSaveReport',` is an ASSIGNMENT and matches neither |

⚠️ A **fourth** instrument did see the block, and that nuance matters for the class:
`check:doc-fences` classifies it as a SYNONYM finding (a TypeScript body under an
unhighlighted fence) and carries it inside a declared SHRINK-ONLY ledger — this page was
baselined at 8 such blocks, and `--list` names our block as one of them
(`content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx:404`). So the block being hidden from the compiler was
a **known, baselined** state, not an unknown one.

### The reading the card asked for

Re-fenced the block `ts` with the two lines **still present**, then ran `check:doc-snippets`:

```
  [semantic]  content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx:421:3  TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'undefined'.
  [semantic]  content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx:422:3  TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'undefined'.
Semantic phase: 457 of 457 block(s) judged, 1 failed.
```

Exactly the two lines this card is about, and nothing else on the page — no other block on
this page uses an ambient name, none continues an earlier block. ⇒ per the dispatch ruling,
**the re-fence lands too**. After the deletion, on the same tree:

```
Covered blocks: 615 — 457 to compile, 158 declared fragment(s).
Semantic phase: 457 of 457 block(s) judged, 0 failed.
Every covered documentation snippet compiles against the built types.
```

456 → 457 compiled blocks: the page has joined the gate's scan surface, so this class is dead
**on this page** by construction — a retired key in a compiled block is a `tsc` error.

## ⚠️ A second file, and why it is not scope creep

`scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs`, one line: `content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx`
8 → 7. The re-fence cannot land without it — that gate went red the moment the block left its
ledger, and it printed its own remedy:

```
❌  check:doc-fences — 1 stale KNOWN_UNHIGHLIGHTED_TS_FENCES entry/entries:
  content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx  — baselined at 8, now carries 7
    Good news, and the list has to say so: lower the numbers in
    KNOWN_UNHIGHLIGHTED_TS_FENCES in scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs
```

That is the lane's documented protocol, stated in the gate's own header: "Every batch of that
lane now lowers these numbers in the same pull request that re-fences the blocks." The number
only ever goes down; no supported route raises it. Repo-wide the ledger moves 90 → 89 blocks.

## ⚠️ The pin that cites this page

`packages/types/src/__tests__/handler-keys-string-any-mirrors-7344.test.ts` cites this page's
`onSave: 'handleSaveReport'` as the corpus source of the retired dialect. Read before
deleting: the citation is a **provenance comment**, and the value is a hard-coded constant —

```
const AUTHORED_STRINGS = ['handleSaveReport', 'toast("Hello from ObjectUI!")'] as const;
```

— while every file that test actually reads comes from `packages/types/src/zod` (its
`ZOD_DIR` walk). It matches by existence-at-authoring-time, never by live content, so the
deletion cannot redden it, and it is green here. ⛔ The pin is not edited. The comment now
cites a page that no longer carries the spelling; that is a historical citation of where the
dialect came from and still reads correctly, so it is reported rather than rewritten.

## Out of scope, filed rather than repaired

objectui#7840 — the objectui#7340 pin cannot see example object literals at all
(`DOC_MEMBER_RE` requires the `?`). Widening it closes the **class** rather than this
instance, but it is its own measurement: the parse surface of example literals is far larger
than that of declaration rows, an owner has to be resolved from a type annotation for the
PAIR RULE to run at all, and the false-positive cost is unmeasured. ⛔ Not attempted here.

## Evidence

Everything below ran on `9d46971b1`, the head of this branch, with the doc gate's scoped
closure built first (`pnpm exec turbo run build $(node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs
--build-filter) --concurrency=2` — 34/34 tasks successful).

| command | verdict |
|:--|:--|
| `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` | exit 0 — "Every covered documentation snippet compiles against the built types." |
| `node scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs` | exit 0 — "✅ Every documented component type is registered." |
| `node scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs` | exit 0 — "every TypeScript block in 227 document(s) is fenced ts/tsx/typescript, except 80 declared file(s) carrying 89 block(s)" |
| `node scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs --self-test` | exit 0 — 26 cases pass |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ scripts/__tests__/check-doc-fence-languages.test.ts scripts/__tests__/check-skill-examples.test.ts scripts/__tests__/one-authority-per-exported-name-6273.test.ts` | exit 0 — Test Files 130 passed (130), Tests 2384 passed (2384) |
| `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` | exit 0 — "Links are valid across 17 scan roots." |
| `node scripts/check-docs-route-eager-closure.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-handler-key-read-sites.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 — 6365 tracked text file(s) scanned |

The three test suites beyond `packages/types` are the ones that name
`check-doc-fence-languages` — a gate script's own suites are owed separately from the gates
its diff triggers.

`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — exit 0, verdict quoted verbatim:

> ✅  No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.

⇒ no changeset file, and ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label: in this repository that label is read
by no workflow and exempts nothing; the gate's own verdict line is the authority.

**Lint, narrowed and proven rather than skipped.** Asked ESLint itself about the two changed
paths, through its own config resolution:

```
content/docs/core/report-schema.mdx     | ignored: true  | has rules: n/a
scripts/check-doc-fence-languages.mjs   | ignored: false | has rules: 0
packages/types/src/reports.ts (control) | ignored: false | has rules: 116
```

The flat config's only file selector is `**/*.{ts,tsx}`, so this diff intersects the linted
population in zero rules; the control shows the query measures something real. And
`tseslint.configs.recommended` is configured with no `project` / `projectService`, so linting
is not type-aware and this diff cannot move the verdict of any file it did not touch.

**Not run, stated plainly:** the full `turbo run lint` and the full test suite (CI runs both);
no browser verification (documentation-only change with no runtime surface); no reverse
ablation beyond the before/after pair above, which is itself the card's required measurement
— every instrument was captured green on the unmodified tree first, which is the point the
card makes.
